library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rantanen_2026_methylprednisolone"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rantanen_2026_methylprednisolone"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00228-026-04168-7> (open access; PMC13486032)

Rantanen and colleagues pooled four prospective Finnish trials of
high-dose methylprednisolone given to neonates and infants at the start of
open-heart surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), and fitted a
population PK model in NONMEM 7.5. Time was modelled in minutes, doses in
mg, concentrations in ng/mL, clearance in L/min and volume in L (Methods,
"Pharmacometric analysis"); the packaged model keeps those units. A
two-compartment model lowered the OFV by about 25 units but did not improve
the diagnostics, so the authors kept the one-compartment model.

# Population

Ninety-three patients contributed 278 plasma concentrations (median three
per patient; Table 1 and Results). Postnatal age was 1-574 days (median 140)
and postmenstrual age 270-854 days (median 424); mean (SD) body weight was
5.8 (1.9) kg, and 53 of 93 were girls. The four cohorts, which are also the
four operation groups of the final model, were:

| Operation group | Study | n | Weight, kg (mean, SD) | Postnatal age, d (median, range) | Dose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OPER 0, neonates (reference) | Keski-Nisula 2013 | 20 | 3.6 (0.41) | 7 (1-27) | 30 mg/kg IV |
| OPER 1, tetralogy of Fallot | Keski-Nisula 2016 | 28 | 7.0 (1.9) | 164 (71-311) | 5 or 30 mg/kg IV, randomized |
| OPER 2, VSD/AVSD | Keski-Nisula 2015 | 30 | 5.8 (1.5) | 144 (98-574) | 30 mg/kg IV or into the CPB prime, randomized |
| OPER 3, Glenn procedure | Keski-Nisula 2020 | 15 | 6.7 (1.1) | 180 (94-371) | 30 mg/kg IV |

Arterial samples were taken 30 min after the start of CPB, 5 min after
protamine and 6 h after the end of CPB, giving sampling times of 23-758 min
after the dose.

```{r population}
pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rantanen_2026_methylprednisolone"))$population
tibble::tibble(
  Field = names(pop),
  Value = vapply(pop, function(x) paste(as.character(x), collapse = "; "), character(1))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Population metadata recorded with the model.")
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` entry in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Rantanen_2026_methylprednisolone.R` carries an
in-file comment giving its source. They are collected here.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| One-compartment model, first-order elimination, IV bolus | -- | Methods "Pharmacometric analysis"; Results "Population pharmacokinetic model" |
| `lcl` (CL at 5.7 kg, PMA 424 d) | log(0.0761 L/min) | Table 2, THETA(1) |
| `lvc` (V at 5.7 kg, OPER 0) | log(27.1 L) | Table 2, THETA(2) |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75, fixed | Table 2, fixed scaling parameters; Methods "Covariate analysis" |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1, fixed | Table 2, fixed scaling parameters; Methods "Covariate analysis" |
| `e_page_cl` | 0.503 | Table 2, THETA(3) |
| `e_study_2008_007413_76_tof_vc` | -0.404 | Table 2, THETA(4) |
| `e_study_2008_007413_76_vsd_avsd_vc` | -0.475 | Table 2, THETA(5) |
| `e_study_2008_007413_76_glenn_vc` | -0.884 | Table 2, THETA(6) |
| `etalcl` variance | 0.208 | Table 2, OMEGA(1,1) |
| `etalvc` variance | 0.0388 | Table 2, OMEGA(2,2) |
| `propSd_neonate` | sqrt(0.0851) = 0.2917 | Table 2, SIGMA(1,1) |
| `propSd_tof` | sqrt(0.179) = 0.4231 | Table 2, SIGMA(2,2) |
| `propSd_vsd_avsd` | sqrt(0.0428) = 0.2069 | Table 2, SIGMA(3,3) |
| `propSd_glenn` | sqrt(0.0197) = 0.1404 | Table 2, SIGMA(4,4) |
| CL = CL_TV (WT/5.7)^0.75 (PMA/424)^theta_PMA | -- | Methods "Covariate analysis", CL equation |
| V = V_TV exp(theta_OPER) (WT/5.7) | -- | Methods "Covariate analysis" (multiplicative log-scale categorical effects); Table 2 |
| theta_i = theta exp(eta_i) | -- | Methods "Pharmacometric analysis" |
| y = ipred (1 + eps_prop), one sigma per operation group | -- | Methods "Pharmacometric analysis"; Table 2 |

## Derived quantities against Table 2

Table 2 reports derived values next to the estimates. They follow from the
packaged parameters:

```{r derived}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rantanen_2026_methylprednisolone"))
th <- mod$theta
om <- mod$omega

derived <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "Typical CL (L/h)",
    "V ratio, tetralogy of Fallot vs neonates",
    "V ratio, VSD/AVSD vs neonates",
    "V ratio, Glenn vs neonates",
    "IIV CV% on CL",
    "IIV CV% on V",
    "Residual SD%, neonates",
    "Residual SD%, tetralogy of Fallot",
    "Residual SD%, VSD/AVSD",
    "Residual SD%, Glenn"
  ),
  Packaged = c(
    exp(th[["lcl"]]) * 60,
    exp(th[["e_study_2008_007413_76_tof_vc"]]),
    exp(th[["e_study_2008_007413_76_vsd_avsd_vc"]]),
    exp(th[["e_study_2008_007413_76_glenn_vc"]]),
    100 * sqrt(exp(om["etalcl", "etalcl"]) - 1),
    100 * sqrt(exp(om["etalvc", "etalvc"]) - 1),
    100 * th[["propSd_neonate"]],
    100 * th[["propSd_tof"]],
    100 * th[["propSd_vsd_avsd"]],
    100 * th[["propSd_glenn"]]
  ),
  Published = c(4.57, 0.668, 0.622, 0.413, 48.1, 19.9, 29.2, 42.3, 20.7, 14.0)
) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (Packaged / Published - 1))

knitr::kable(derived, digits = 3, caption = "Derived values: packaged model versus Table 2 and Results text.")

# Same-parameter arithmetic: only rounding of the published figures separates them.
stopifnot(all(abs(derived$`Difference (%)`) < 0.5))
```

# Virtual cohort

Each operation group is drawn from its Table 1 summary. Weight is normal
with the published mean and SD, truncated to plausible bounds; postnatal age
is log-normal around the published median and truncated to the published
range. Postmenstrual age follows the paper: the neonatal cohort's PMA is
drawn directly from its 270-316 day range, and the other cohorts are given
PMA = 280 days + postnatal age (Table 1, footnote a). PMA is converted to
months for the canonical `PAGE` column.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20260818)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260818)

draw_trunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, mean, sd), lo), hi)
}

draw_pna <- function(n, median, lo, hi) {
  pmin(pmax(median * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.45)), lo), hi)
}

n_per <- 100L

groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,           ~wt_mean, ~wt_sd, ~pna_med, ~pna_lo, ~pna_hi, ~tof, ~vsd_avsd, ~glenn,
  "Neonates",       3.6,      0.41,   7,        1,       27,      0,    0,         0,
  "TOF",            7.0,      1.9,    164,      71,      311,     1,    0,         0,
  "VSD/AVSD",       5.8,      1.5,    144,      98,      574,     0,    1,         0,
  "Glenn",          6.7,      1.1,    180,      94,      371,     0,    0,         1
)

make_group <- function(row, id_offset) {
  pna <- draw_pna(n_per, row$pna_med, row$pna_lo, row$pna_hi)
  pma_days <- if (row$group == "Neonates") {
    stats::runif(n_per, 270, 316)
  } else {
    280 + pna
  }
  # The tetralogy of Fallot trial randomized 5 versus 30 mg/kg; the other
  # cohorts all received 30 mg/kg.
  dose_mgkg <- if (row$group == "TOF") rep(c(5, 30), length.out = n_per) else rep(30, n_per)
  tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_per),
    group = row$group,
    dose_mgkg = dose_mgkg,
    WT = draw_trunc_norm(n_per, row$wt_mean, row$wt_sd, 2.5, 13),
    PAGE = pma_days / 30.4375,
    STUDY_2008_007413_76_TOF = row$tof,
    STUDY_2008_007413_76_VSD_AVSD = row$vsd_avsd,
    STUDY_2008_007413_76_GLENN = row$glenn
  )
}

subjects <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(groups)), function(i) {
  make_group(groups[i, ], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per)
})) |>
  mutate(
    treatment = ifelse(group == "TOF", paste0(group, " ", dose_mgkg, " mg/kg"), group),
    amt = dose_mgkg * WT
  )
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(subjects$id))

obs_times <- c(0, seq(5, 720, by = 5))

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  subjects |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"),
  subjects |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

subjects |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    `WT mean (kg)` = mean(WT),
    `PMA median (d)` = median(PAGE * 30.4375),
    `Dose mean (mg)` = mean(amt)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort by operation group.")
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events,
  keep = c("group", "treatment", "WT", "dose_mgkg")
) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Typical values: omega = NA and sigma = NA solve with every eta and epsilon at
# zero. zeroRe() is avoided because it shares state with the population solve
# above.
sim_typ <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events,
  omega = NA, sigma = NA,
  keep = c("group", "treatment", "WT", "dose_mgkg")
)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1: observed concentration-time profiles

Figure 1 of Rantanen 2026 plots all 278 observed concentrations against time
after the dose. The maintainers digitised the figure (274 of the 278 points
were recovered; a few overlap) and summarised the observations by time
window. The simulated cohort, with residual error, is summarised over the
same windows.

```{r fig1, fig.cap = "Simulated observations at the protocol sampling windows (replicates the layout of Figure 1 of Rantanen 2026)."}
sample_windows <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% c(seq(30, 240, by = 5), seq(400, 720, by = 5))) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  slice_sample(n = 3) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(sample_windows, aes(time, sim, group = id, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 800), ylim = c(0, 15000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (min)",
    y = "Methylprednisolone Cp (ng/mL)",
    colour = "Operation group"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig1-windows}
# Digitised from Figure 1 of Rantanen 2026: number of observations and their
# median (ng/mL) in each time window.
fig1_obs <- tibble::tibble(
  window = c("(0,100]", "(100,200]", "(200,300]", "(300,450]", "(450,600]", "(600,800]"),
  n_obs = c(53, 92, 33, 18, 63, 15),
  obs_median = c(6966, 5646, 4622, 1668, 885, 901)
)

window_breaks <- c(0, 100, 200, 300, 450, 600, 800)

fig1_sim <- sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  mutate(window = as.character(cut(time, window_breaks))) |>
  group_by(window) |>
  summarise(sim_median = median(sim), .groups = "drop")

fig1_check <- dplyr::inner_join(fig1_obs, fig1_sim, by = "window") |>
  mutate(ratio = sim_median / obs_median)

fig1_check |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time window (min)" = window,
    "Observed n" = n_obs,
    "Observed median (ng/mL)" = obs_median,
    "Simulated median (ng/mL)" = sim_median,
    "Simulated / observed" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated versus digitised observed medians by time window (Figure 1).")

# Windows with at least 30 observations. The simulated cohort samples every
# subject uniformly in time, while the trials sampled at CPB-anchored times that
# differ by cohort, so only agreement within two-fold is asserted; a unit slip in
# CL or V moves these medians by an order of magnitude.
fig1_main <- dplyr::filter(fig1_check, n_obs >= 30)
stopifnot(
  nrow(fig1_main) == 4L,
  all(fig1_main$ratio > 0.5 & fig1_main$ratio < 2)
)
```

## Figure 4: prediction-corrected VPC

Figure 4 is a prediction-corrected VPC of all four cohorts, plotted in hours
on a log scale. Its simulated median falls from about 8000 ng/mL at 0.5 h to
about 950 ng/mL at 15 h (read off the figure by the maintainers). Prediction
correction rescales each observation to the median population prediction of
its time bin, so in the wide late bins the corrected values sit above the
raw concentrations: Figure 1's raw observations at 450-600 min have a median
near 900 ng/mL, while Figure 4 plots about 2000 ng/mL at 8 h. The
uncorrected simulated median below therefore matches Figure 4 early and
falls below it late; it is shown for orientation, and the quantitative check
is the one against Figure 1 above.

```{r fig4, fig.cap = "Pooled 5th/50th/95th percentiles of the simulated cohort (not prediction-corrected) with the Figure 4 simulated median (points) of Rantanen 2026."}
fig4_median <- tibble::tibble(
  time_h = c(0.5, 2, 4, 8, 15),
  conc = c(8000, 5500, 3900, 2000, 950)
)

pooled <- sim |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    p50 = median(sim),
    p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(time_h = time / 60)

ggplot(pooled, aes(time_h)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = fig4_median, aes(time_h, conc), colour = "red", size = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Methylprednisolone concentration (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r typical, fig.cap = "Typical-value concentration-time profiles for each operation group at its cohort's simulated weight and age."}
sim_typ |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(Cc = median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +

```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. The check below runs PKNCA on the typical-value
(no random effects) simulation and compares each operation group's AUC and
half-life with the closed-form one-compartment values computed from the same
covariates: AUC = dose / CL and t1/2 = ln 2 V / CL.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_sim <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

# Closed form, per subject, from the same covariates and typical parameters
closed <- subjects |>
  mutate(
    cl = exp(th[["lcl"]]) * (WT / 5.7)^0.75 * (PAGE * 30.4375 / 424)^th[["e_page_cl"]],
    vc = exp(th[["lvc"]] +
      th[["e_study_2008_007413_76_tof_vc"]] * STUDY_2008_007413_76_TOF +
      th[["e_study_2008_007413_76_vsd_avsd_vc"]] * STUDY_2008_007413_76_VSD_AVSD +
      th[["e_study_2008_007413_76_glenn_vc"]] * STUDY_2008_007413_76_GLENN) * (WT / 5.7),
    aucinf.obs = 1000 * amt / cl,
    half.life = log(2) * vc / cl
  ) |>
  select(treatment, id, aucinf.obs, half.life) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(aucinf.obs, half.life), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "closed")

nca_chk <- dplyr::inner_join(nca_sim, closed, by = c("treatment", "id", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / closed - 1))

# Same parameters on both sides: only extrapolation and trapezoid error differ.
stopifnot(
  nrow(nca_chk) == 2L * nrow(subjects),
  abs(median(nca_chk$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(nca_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)

nca_simulated <- nca_sim |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
nca_reference <- closed |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = median(closed), .groups = "drop")

nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_simulated,
  reference = nca_reference,
  by = "treatment"
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median PKNCA AUC0-inf (min*ng/mL) and half-life (min) versus the closed-form one-compartment values, by operation group.")
```

The half-lives range from roughly 1.7 h in the Glenn cohort (smallest
volume) to over 4 h in neonates (lowest clearance, set by both weight and
postmenstrual age).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Operation-group indicators.** The source covariate `OPER` (0 = neonates,
  1 = tetralogy of Fallot, 2 = VSD/AVSD, 3 = Glenn) is carried as three
  binary study indicators, `STUDY_2008_007413_76_TOF`,
  `STUDY_2008_007413_76_VSD_AVSD` and `STUDY_2008_007413_76_GLENN`, with the
  neonatal cohort as the reference when all three are 0. Each operation group
  is one source trial, and the authors caution that the group effects on V
  mix developmental, anatomical and perioperative differences (Discussion),
  so the maintainers carry them as study indicators rather than as
  procedure-type covariates. All four trials were registered under the one
  EudraCT number 2008-007413-76 (Methods; EU Clinical Trials Register,
  sponsor protocol code "steroiditutkimus", checked 2026-11-22), so the
  indicator names combine that number with the cohort label.
* **Per-group residual error.** The paper estimated "separate residual error
  models ... for each study"; Table 2 labels the four sigmas by operation
  group. Because each study is one operation group, the residual SD is
  selected by the same indicators.
* **Postmenstrual age units.** The source centres PMA in days on 424 days.
  The packaged model takes the canonical `PAGE` column in months and converts
  with 30.4375 days per month inside `model()`.
* **Units.** Time is in minutes and CL in L/min, as the source fitted them.
  Concentration is returned in ng/mL (dose in mg divided by V in L, times
  1000).
* **Route.** Doses given into the CPB-circuit priming solution were modelled
  as intravenous boluses by the authors and are dosed into `central` here.
* **Virtual cohort.** Weight and postnatal-age distributions within each
  cohort are reconstructed from the Table 1 summaries (mean/SD for weight,
  median/range for age); the individual data are not published. The
  tetralogy of Fallot cohort is split evenly between 5 and 30 mg/kg because
  the number given each dose is not reported.
* **Figure comparisons.** The Figure 1 window medians come from the
  maintainers' digitisation of the published scatter (274 of 278 points
  recovered) and the Figure 4 median points were read off the figure; both
  are approximate. Figure 4 is prediction-corrected and is shown for
  orientation only.
* **Errata.** Europe PMC lists no erratum or correction for this article (checked
  2026-11-16).
